newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-B.A.T puts, calls sold for premium.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-B.A.T puts, calls sold for premium.

text.p: A swarm of trades were made on Thursday in options of tobacco-to-insurance group B.A.T Industries, dealers said.

This followed yesterday's news from the U.S. about talks for a possible settlement of litigation with the tobacco industry and most of the deals were from sellers of puts and calls believing that volatility in B.A.T will fall in the weeks ahead.
Attention was concentrated in the July 550 puts and calls which were sold at prices around 32p and 34p respectively in short straddle deals with lot sizes of up to 400 contracts.
By 1400 GMT, B.A.T shares were down 4p to 537p.
For maximum profit at expiry from the short straddles the shares need to be exactly 550p because that's when the puts and calls will be worthless and the full premiums can be collected.
Over 2,600 July 550 calls had been traded and almost 2,000 July 550 puts -- the imbalnce was due to other traders taking separate positions.

In food and drinks group Grand Metropolitan the main deal was also a short straddle consisting of the sale of 500 August 500 puts and calls at 23p and 26p each. A further 250 lots were sold in a separate deal and at the same prices.
Volatility was also sold in aero-engine manufacturer Rolls Royce where 250 August 240 puts were sold at 12p along with 250 August 260 calls at 11p in a short strangle strategy.

In this case because of the different strike prices the seller can make a maximum profit -- of 23p -- over a wider range than from a short straddle. For maximum profit the shares need to be anywhere between 240p and 260p at expiry.
Rolls Royce shares were unchanged at 247p.
There was also a seller of 500 July 160 puts at 21-1/2p in British Steel. The shares added 1-1/2p to 148-1/4p.
